name: Sales & Retail
tagline: Invoices, reps, territories, margins, targets and the deal pipeline
description: Invoice and order-line exports from ERP, billing and POS tools (Tally, Zoho Books, SAP, QuickBooks, Vyapar, store POS) and opportunity exports from CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho CRM, Pipedrive).

fields.label: Invoice number
fields.description: Identifies each invoice or order; repeats on every line of a multi-line invoice.

fields.label: Customer
fields.description: The buying customer or account: a code or a name.

fields.label: Customer name
fields.description: Second customer column (a name next to a customer code); used when no customer ID is mapped.

fields.label: Beat / route
fields.description: The salesman's beat: the fixed round of retail outlets a distributor's salesman visits.

fields.label: Store / branch
fields.description: The shop, branch, outlet or showroom where the sale was made.

fields.label: Till / POS terminal
fields.description: The cash register, till, billing counter or POS terminal that rang up the bill.

fields.label: Cashier
fields.description: The staff member who billed the sale at the counter.

fields.label: Payment mode
fields.description: How the customer paid at the counter: cash, card, UPI, wallet, cheque or credit.

fields.label: Unit price
fields.description: Price per unit before the line discount (list or invoice rate).

fields.label: Discount %
fields.description: Line discount as a fraction of the gross line value (0.10 = 10%).

fields.label: Discount amount
fields.description: Value given away as discount on the line. A Discount column holding fractions (0.2 = 20%) belongs in Discount %.

fields.label: Gross amount
fields.description: Line value before discount (quantity × list price).

fields.label: Revenue / amount
fields.description: Net revenue on an invoice or order line (after discount, before tax), or the deal value on a CRM opportunity.

fields.label: Tax / GST
fields.description: Tax charged on the line or bill (GST, VAT or sales tax); revenue is measured before it.

fields.label: HSN / SAC code
fields.description: The GST goods (HSN) or services (SAC) code printed on a B2B tax invoice line.

fields.label: Sales target
fields.description: Target or quota, one value per rep (or territory) and period.

fields.label: Bills / transactions
fields.description: A count of bills (transactions, receipts) already totalled per store, day or week, as store summaries report it.

fields.label: Like-for-like growth %
fields.description: Sales growth of stores open in both periods, as a store league table reports it.

fields.label: Win probability
fields.description: Probability of winning the deal as a fraction (0.4 = 40%).

subDomains.name: Invoices & order lines
subDomains.description: One row per invoice or order line with customer, product, quantity and value.

subDomains.name: CRM pipeline
subDomains.description: One row per opportunity with stage, amount, owner and close date.

subDomains.name: Store & POS sales
subDomains.description: One row per bill or bill line from a shop's till, with the store, till or cashier and payment mode; or a store summary of sales and bill counts.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.definition: Net sales value invoiced in the period, after line discounts and before tax.
kpis.formula: Sum of line revenue (net of discount, excluding tax)

variants.label: Gross amount − discount amount
variants.caveat: No revenue column, so revenue is gross amount minus discount amount.

variants.label: Quantity × unit price × (1 − discount %)
variants.caveat: No revenue column, so revenue is rebuilt from quantity, unit price and the line discount %.

variants.label: Gross amount (no discount data)
variants.caveat: No revenue or discount column, so revenue equals the gross amount.

variants.label: Quantity × unit price
variants.caveat: No revenue or discount column, so revenue is quantity × unit price before any discount.

pitfalls: Returns and credit notes should be negative lines; cancelled invoices left in the file overstate revenue.

kpis.name: Gross sales
kpis.definition: Sales value at list or invoice price, before discounts.
kpis.formula: Gross amount, or revenue + discounts, or quantity × unit price

variants.label: Revenue + discount amount
variants.caveat: No gross amount column, so gross sales are revenue plus discounts.

variants.label: Quantity × unit price
variants.caveat: Rebuilt as quantity × unit price; if the price is already net of discount, discounts read as zero.

variants.label: Revenue ÷ (1 − discount %), line by line
variants.caveat: Grossed up line by line from revenue and the discount %; lines with a 100% discount drop out.

kpis.name: Discounts given
kpis.definition: Value given away as line discounts, schemes and markdowns.
kpis.formula: Sum of discount amount (or quantity × unit price × discount %)

variants.label: Quantity × unit price × discount %
variants.caveat: No discount amount column, so discounts are rebuilt from quantity, unit price and the line discount %.

variants.label: Revenue × discount % ÷ (1 − discount %)
variants.caveat: Derived line by line from revenue and the discount %.

variants.label: Gross sales − revenue
variants.caveat: Derived as gross sales minus revenue, so it also includes any other deductions.

kpis.name: Discount %
kpis.definition: Share of gross sales given away as discounts, weighted by line value.
pitfalls: Averaging the line Discount % column overweights small lines; this is a value-weighted ratio of sums.

kpis.name: Units sold
kpis.definition: Total quantity sold.
pitfalls: Quantities only add up within one unit of measure; mixing pieces, cases and kilograms makes the total meaningless.

kpis.name: Invoices
kpis.definition: Number of distinct invoices or orders raised.

variants.label: Row count (no invoice number)
variants.caveat: No invoice number, so every row is counted as one invoice. Check the grain.

kpis.name: Average invoice value
kpis.definition: Revenue earned per invoice.
kpis.formula: Revenue ÷ invoices (ratio of sums, not an average of invoice totals)
pitfalls: A few very large invoices can lift the average while most invoices shrink; read it next to the invoice count.

kpis.name: Average selling price
kpis.definition: Revenue earned per unit sold, weighted by quantity.
pitfalls: A shift in product mix moves ASP even when no price changed (mix effect).

kpis.name: Gross profit
kpis.definition: Revenue left after the cost of the goods sold, on lines that carry a cost.

variants.label: Profit column
variants.caveat: No cost column, so the file's own profit column is used.

variants.label: Revenue − total cost
variants.caveat: Revenue is rebuilt from price and quantity, so lines without a cost still count their revenue.

variants.label: Revenue − quantity × unit cost
variants.caveat: Cost is rebuilt as quantity × unit cost.

pitfalls: Lines without a cost are left out, so gross profit understates the total when many lines lack costs; check cost coverage first.

kpis.name: Gross margin %
kpis.definition: Share of revenue kept after the cost of goods, measured on lines that carry a cost.
kpis.formula: Σ (revenue − cost) ÷ Σ revenue, over lines with a cost

variants.label: Σ(revenue − cost) ÷ Σ revenue on costed lines
Σ profit ÷ Σ revenue
variants.caveat: No cost column, so the file's own profit column is used.

variants.label: Gross profit ÷ revenue
variants.caveat: Measured on total revenue, including any lines without a cost.

pitfalls: Margin gaps between reps or regions often reflect product mix rather than pricing (Simpson's paradox); compare within a category.

kpis.name: Customers
kpis.definition: Distinct customers invoiced in the period.

variants.label: Distinct customer names
variants.caveat: Counted by name, so spelling variants of one customer count separately.

kpis.name: Revenue per customer
kpis.definition: Average revenue from each customer invoiced in the period.
pitfalls: Short periods show lower revenue per customer because each customer has had fewer chances to buy.

kpis.name: New customers
kpis.definition: Customers whose first invoice in the file falls in the period.
kpis.formula: Customers with first invoice date ≥ period start

variants.label: First invoice in period (by name)
variants.caveat: Customers are identified by name.

pitfalls: Customers who bought before the file starts look new; the longer the history, the more accurate this is.

kpis.name: Repeat customer rate
kpis.definition: Share of the period's customers who bought on two or more separate invoices.

variants.label: Customers (by name) with 2+ invoices ÷ customers
variants.caveat: Customers are identified by name.

pitfalls: Depends on the window: a one-month view always shows a lower repeat rate than a full year.

kpis.name: Revenue per sales rep
kpis.definition: Revenue divided by the number of reps who invoiced in the period.
pitfalls: Reps who joined or left mid-period count as a full rep; compare complete periods.

kpis.name: Target attainment %
kpis.definition: Revenue achieved as a share of the sales target.
pitfalls: A target repeated on every invoice line is summed many times; the target column must hold one value per rep and period.

kpis.name: Bills
kpis.definition: Number of bills (receipts or transactions) rung up in the period.

variants.label: Bill-count column
variants.caveat: No bill number, so bills are the file's own bill-count column, summed.

variants.label: Row count (no bill number)
variants.caveat: No bill number, so every row is counted as one bill. Check the grain.

pitfalls: A bill-line export repeats the bill number on every line: bills are counted with DISTINCT, never by counting rows.

kpis.name: Average bill value
kpis.definition: Revenue per bill: what a customer spends in one visit.
kpis.formula: Revenue ÷ bills (ratio of sums, not an average of bill totals)
pitfalls: A rise can come from fewer small bills rather than bigger baskets; read it next to the bill count.

kpis.name: Units per bill
kpis.definition: Items sold per bill: the size of the average basket.
pitfalls: Units only add up within one unit of measure; goods sold loose by weight inflate units per bill.

kpis.name: Stores
kpis.definition: Distinct stores, branches or outlets that made a sale in the period.

kpis.name: Sales per store
kpis.definition: Revenue per store that traded in the period.
pitfalls: A store that opened, closed or was refitted during the period counts as a full store; compare stores open throughout.

kpis.name: Card & UPI share
kpis.definition: Share of bills paid by card, UPI or a mobile wallet rather than cash or credit.
kpis.formula: Bills paid by card, UPI or wallet ÷ bills with a payment mode

variants.label: Card, UPI or wallet bills ÷ bills with a payment mode
Card, UPI or wallet rows ÷ rows with a payment mode
variants.caveat: No bill number, so each row is counted as one bill.

pitfalls: A bill paid partly in cash and partly by card counts in both groups when the export lists each payment on its own row.

kpis.name: Open pipeline
kpis.definition: Value of deals not yet won or lost.
kpis.formula: Sum of deal amount where the stage is neither won nor lost
pitfalls: Pipeline describes the day of the export; stale deals with past close dates inflate it.

kpis.name: Weighted pipeline
kpis.definition: Open deal value weighted by each deal's win probability: the expected value of the open pipeline.
kpis.formula: Σ (deal amount × probability) over open deals

variants.label: Σ amount × probability on open deals
Weighted amount column on open deals
variants.caveat: No probability column, so the CRM's own weighted (expected revenue) column is used.

pitfalls: Probability must be a fraction (0.4 = 40%); a CRM export in points (40) overstates this a hundredfold.
Stage probabilities are often defaults rather than judgements; treat the weighted figure as a rough forecast.

kpis.name: Won revenue
kpis.definition: Value of deals closed as won.
kpis.formula: Sum of deal amount where the stage is won

kpis.name: Deals won
kpis.definition: Number of distinct deals closed as won.

variants.label: Won rows
variants.caveat: No opportunity ID, so each won row counts as one deal.

kpis.name: Win rate
kpis.definition: Share of closed deals that were won, by count.

variants.label: Won ÷ (won + lost) rows
variants.caveat: No opportunity ID, so rows are counted as deals.

benchmark.note: Indicative B2B range that is often quoted; it depends heavily on how early deals are logged as opportunities.

pitfalls: Open deals are left out, so a period full of young deals can show a high win rate on very few closures.

kpis.name: Average deal size
kpis.definition: Won revenue per won deal.

kpis.name: Sales cycle
kpis.definition: Average calendar days from deal creation to close, for won deals.
kpis.formula: Average of (close date − created date) over won deals

variants.label: Close − created date, all deals with both dates
variants.caveat: No won stage recognised, so every deal with both dates counts (open deals use their expected close date).

pitfalls: A few very long deals pull the average up; compare reps on similar deal sizes.

kpis.name: Deal value (all stages)
kpis.definition: Total value of every deal in view, whatever its stage.

charts.title: Revenue over time
charts.reason: One measure over a continuous time axis reads best as a line; the soft fill emphasises volume without hiding the shape.

charts.title: Revenue by customer segment
charts.reason: Revenue adds up across segments, so stacked monthly columns show the total and the segment mix in one view.

charts.title: Revenue by sales rep
charts.reason: One measure compared across named reps: sorted horizontal bars keep names readable. Top 15 plus Others.

charts.title: Revenue by category
charts.reason: Comparing one measure across named categories: sorted horizontal bars, top 10 plus Others, with drill-down to products.

charts.title: Revenue by region
charts.reason: Territories compared on one measure: sorted bars make the biggest and smallest regions obvious.

charts.title: Gross margin by discount depth
charts.reason: Do deeper discounts erode margin? The margin recomputed for each discount band, shown in band order.

charts.title: Customer concentration (Pareto)
charts.reason: How dependent revenue is on a few accounts: each customer's share as columns and the cumulative share as a line on one 0–100% axis.

charts.title: Reps: revenue vs gross margin
charts.reason: Two measures per rep: a scatter with a trendline separates reps who buy volume with discounts from those who sell at healthy margins.

charts.title: Top products
charts.reason: Several measures per product: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

charts.title: Average bill value over time
charts.reason: ABV is a ratio, so it is plotted as a line of the ratio recomputed for each period, never summed.

charts.title: Revenue by store
charts.reason: One measure compared across named stores: sorted horizontal bars rank them and keep names readable. Top 15 plus Others.

charts.title: Bills by payment mode
charts.reason: Part-to-whole with a handful of payment modes: a donut shows the cash, card and UPI split at a glance.

charts.title: Average bill value by store
charts.reason: A ratio compared across stores: ABV recomputed for each store and sorted; stores with under 30 lines are hidden as too few to judge.

charts.title: When customers shop
charts.reason: Two time dimensions and one count: a heatmap of weekday × hour shows the busy hours to staff for.

charts.title: Store scorecard
charts.reason: Several measures per store side by side: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

charts.title: Top products
charts.reason: Several measures per product, including how many bills each one was on: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

charts.title: Won revenue by close month
charts.reason: Bookings over a continuous time axis: an area of won value per close month shows momentum and seasonality.

charts.title: Deal value by stage
charts.reason: Where the money sits: deal value per stage as sorted bars, with won and lost shown for context.

charts.title: Win rate by rep
charts.reason: A rate compared across reps: the win rate recomputed per rep and sorted; reps with fewer than 20 deals are hidden as too few to judge.

pitfalls: Invoice exports repeat the invoice number on every line: invoices and customers are counted with DISTINCT, never by counting rows.
Average invoice value, ASP, margin %, discount % and win rate are recomputed from totals for every period and segment; they are never averaged across rows or summed.
Returns and credit notes must appear as negative lines and cancelled invoices must be removed; otherwise revenue is overstated.
Margin differences between reps or regions often reflect product mix rather than selling skill (Simpson's paradox); compare within a category before drawing conclusions.
Targets usually live at rep × month grain; joined onto every invoice line they are summed many times and attainment collapses.
Pipeline figures describe the day the CRM was exported; stale deals with past close dates and default stage probabilities make open and weighted pipeline look bigger than reality.
